Blur to Shut Down Frontend and Stop Matching New Blend Loans on November 12; BLUR Plunges Over 16% NFT marketplace Blur announced it will shut down its frontend on November 12, 2026, while its onchain marketplace protocol will remain operational and BLUR will continue to control the protocol's fee switch. Its NFT lending protocol, Blend, will stop matching new loans on the same date. Borrowers have until then to repay their loans or allow them to default. Blur will subsequently provide a frontend tool for users to withdraw their assets from Blend. Following the announcement, BLUR plunged to a low of 0.01410 USDT before recovering to 0.01523 USDT, down 16.55% over 24 hours, per Binance data. Blur raised $11 million in a seed funding round in March 2022, with investors including Paradigm, eGirl Capital, and 0xMaki. — link

TOKEN2049 Side Event Organizers Reported to Singapore Police for Allegedly Forcing Remote-Access Software Installs According to SolanaFloor, an attendee filed a police report with the Singapore Police stating that organizers operating under the names “Apex Accelerator” and “Stone Venture” promoted a crypto security event called “Don’t Get Played” during TOKEN2049 week. They allegedly pressured attendees to install software that gave the organizers remote control of their computers. — link

South Korea Orders Website Blocks on 27 Unregistered Overseas Crypto Exchanges, Including KuCoin, MEXC and BingX South Korea's Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) announced that the country's communications review authority has ordered domestic access restrictions on 27 unregistered overseas cryptocurrency exchange websites, including KuCoin, MEXC, Phemex, XT com, Bitrue, CoinW, Poloniex, BTCC, BingX and BitMart, according to Etoday. The decision, made following reviews on October 6–7, expands existing restrictions on app downloads and updates to exchange websites. The FIU has referred 44 unregistered virtual asset service providers to investigative authorities and plans to seek additional blocks on alternative domains used to circumvent the restrictions. Authorities said they would also provide withdrawal guidance to affected users through DAXA. — link

Highlight Clip: Bloomberg Strategist: Bitcoin Has Become a "Stock-Market Puppet" Bloomberg Strategist: Bitcoin Has Become a "Stock-Market Puppet" Bloomberg Intelligence Senior Commodity Strategist Mike McGlone said in an October 1 interview with Wealthion that Bitcoin's high correlation with U.S. equities, combined with its greater volatility, has made it increasingly look like a "stock-market puppet." He noted that Bitcoin is down about 4% this year while the S&P 500 is up around 3%, and that Bitcoin has also lagged the stock market for nearly five years. McGlone added that he still stands by his view that Bitcoin could fall to $10,000 and sees no reason yet to abandon that call. He also said the broader crypto market remains in the process of a "purge." — link
